reference.kind: norm: published fits of the Galactic disk mass function (recalled, tier T2, until a lane reads the papers); no generator run sets a range
reference.point: the default galaxy's reference solar position (tests.audit.prevalence_stars.solar_populations)
reference.note: A bin's range is the lowest and the highest share the named curves give it, widened by the relative tolerance and then by four binomial sigma of the run. The two samples answer two questions: what the generator draws as the primary of a system (compared with the system function), and what its systems hold in all (compared with the single-star function). Below 0.8 solar masses every star born is still alive, so the born shares are the present shares; above it the sample is the living stars of the population model and the rows only report what the generator makes (no norm yet).

anomaly_notes.GEN.951: the primary function is derived from the single-star function and the companion draw (a flat mass ratio of 0.1 to 1, GEN.928); the system function ([R0705], centre 0.22 solar masses) has 7.7 to 12% of the primaries at 0.6 to 0.8 solar masses and the derivation 6.8%: too many companions fall there from the 0.8 to 1.5 solar mass primaries, where the observed mass ratios peak low and have a twin excess ([R3108], GEN.951)
anomaly_notes.GEN.996: white dwarfs come from single stars only, by the [R0961] initial-final mass relation over the generator's ages: mean mass 0.703 solar masses against 0.55 to 0.70 observed; binary evolution makes low-mass (helium core, about 0.4) white dwarfs, which the generator does not draw
